messages:
maya: heads-up, found possible SSRF in the profile bulk fetch endpoint. quick PoC below, returns internal metadata when image_url points at metadata IP :eyes:

maya: PoC:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/api/v1/profiles/bulk_fetch \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <svc-token>' \\n  -d '{"ids": [123,456], "image_url": "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/"}'
```

maya: response is 200 and includes the fetched body (so the service is proxying arbitrary URLs). notably, requests to internal hostnames (10.0.0.0/8) return service-internal html and small JSON with host metadata.

sam: wow. severity? can you confirm this leaks creds or tokens, or just metadata?

maya: initial check: metadata endpoint returned role name and a bunch of lines that look like credential fragments. i masked out most, but looks like temporary creds were exposed in the response object. attaching clipped response below:

maya: clipped response: `{ "fetched": "...role-name\n\{\"AccessKeyId\":\"ASIA...\",\"SecretAccessKey\":\"...\"... }" }`

nora: stepping in for containment. immediate actions i'm proposing:
- block outbound HTTP(s) egress to 169.254.169.254 and private CIDRs at the WAF / edge LB layer
- disable /api/v1/profiles/bulk_fetch in prod (feature flag) until patched
- remove any cached responses from the service caches

ash: agreed. i'll push a WAF rule to block requests where image_url resolves to private ranges. we should also add network egress deny for metadata IP at VPC firewall level (infra ticket).

linh: i can do a quick app change to validate image_url and reject if host resolves to private or link-local. quick fix: resolve hostname at request time and check against allowlist, no redirects allowed, and set a 2s timeout. i can ship to canary in 15m and roll to prod after smoke.

sam: also: rotate any AWS temporary creds that may have been exposed and force rotate the service principal used by profile-service. security checklist: rotate keys, revoke active tokens, rotate KMS key access policy for that service principal, enable audit logs for the service. someone from infra to coordinate with AWS console?

ash: infra, please confirm we can revoke the role/sessions and rotate the role's credentials. i'll open infra ticket INFRA-7269 and assign to cloud-ops now.

maya: we've started a lightweight detection rule: log requests to bulk_fetch where image_url contains ip literals or known internal hostnames, send to sec-alerts channel. please enable request-body logging for the next 48h for that route (only headers+url previously logged). aware of PII risk but we need exploit detection.

nora: agree to temporary increased logging. ensure logs go to secure bucket with 90d retention and restricted ACLs. add note to redact any tokens in logs automatically.

incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-042: "profile-bulk-fetch SSRF -> potential creds exposure". Severity: high. Pager duty: on-call sec + cloud-ops.

sam: comms: we need legal + privacy loop, CS note draft (no PII, high-level), and decide whether to notify customers. for now treat as internal breach until we have rotated creds.

linh: quick mitigation deployed to canary (canary-3) 10:02am, validation added, returns 400 for private ranges and logs block_reason. running smoke.

maya: thanks. i will run a quick sweep of logs to enumerate suspicious callers and timestamps and share list to the incident ticket.

ash: infra confirms they can revoke sessions and will rotate the role tomorrow at 09:00 UTC. they asked if we need emergency rotation now — sam/nora?

sam: do emergency rotation now. any exposed creds must be considered compromised. schedule coordination: rotate role + revoke sessions immediately, then rotate KMS key binding for the service within 24h.

nora: i'll prepare the post-incident checklist. immediate action items summarized for clarity:
- [x] block egress to metadata IP + private CIDRs at WAF (ash)
- [x] disable endpoint behind feature flag (nora)
- [x] quick app validation deployed to canary (linh)
- [x] rotate exposed service role credentials (infra)
- [x] enable temporary request-body logging for route (maya)
- [x] create detection alert and hunt logs (maya)
- [ ] customer/legal comms draft (sam, nora)
- [ ] full postmortem and timeline (owner: nora)

maya: i'll drop raw findings into the incident ticket and follow-up with IPs/caller ids. thanks all. :thumbsup:
